record.label: Neurosymbolic AI, plain definition
record.statement: Neurosymbolic AI wires a neural component (a learned model: flexible, fast, sometimes wrong, cannot show its work) to a symbolic component (explicit rules, logic, or math: rigid and laborious to build, but exact and mechanically checkable) so that each covers the other's weakness.

record.label: LLM-proposes / symbolic-disposes pattern
record.statement: In all four repositories the language model suggests a move (an answer, a query step, a piece of code) and a mechanical component (a prover, a simulator, a schema check) accepts or rejects it; the phrase adapts the proverb 'man proposes, God disposes'. Where the mechanical verdict sits, and whether anything enforces it, is what distinguishes the four.

record.label: Knockout as clamping
record.statement: A gene knockout is simulated by fixing one substance's concentration at zero and holding it there, then running the model twice, with and without the knockout, and diffing the two time courses: unplug one machine on the factory line and watch which shelves go empty downstream.

record.label: Metabolic control analysis (MCA)
record.statement: Metabolic control analysis measures how much control each individual reaction step has over the whole pathway's output: it finds the bottleneck quantitatively instead of by intuition, asking of every machine on the line 'if this one ran 1% faster, how much more would the line produce?'.

record.label: Scaled sensitivity analysis
record.statement: Sensitivity analysis nudges each model parameter slightly and measures how much the output moves per unit of nudge; large ratios mark the dials that matter and small ones the dials that are decoration.

record.label: Pulse response
record.statement: Pulse response injects a sudden burst of a substance into the simulated system and watches how every concentration reacts and recovers over time: kick the system once, cleanly, and read its character from the ringing.

record.label: COPASI, the simulator
record.statement: COPASI is an established open-source biochemical pathway simulator: given a published model of a cell's reaction network (which substances react with which, at what rates), it computes how concentrations evolve over time. In the pipeline it is the calculator, not an AI, and its numbers are the only part nobody can argue with.

record.label: kiro-cli, the coding agent
record.statement: kiro-cli is AWS's terminal coding agent, their counterpart to Claude Code. Two of the four repositories shell out to it as the component that writes and repairs code, invoked headless with all tool permissions trusted.

record.label: Description logic and reasoners
record.statement: Description logic is a deliberately restricted logic for defining categories and their relations ('every X is a kind of Y', 'X has part Z'), restricted precisely so that a program called a reasoner can mechanically derive every consequence and detect every contradiction. Large medical vocabularies such as SNOMED CT are written in it. Owning a DL ontology without running a reasoner is owning a family tree and never inferring who is whose cousin.

record.label: SMT solver / theorem prover (cvc5)
record.statement: cvc5 is an SMT solver, a program that takes formal statements and either proves that one follows from the others or produces a counterexample. Its answer is a proof, not a probability: where an LLM says 'this looks right', cvc5 says 'this cannot be false, here is why', or 'here is a world where it breaks'.

record.label: Domain Relational Calculus (DRC)
record.statement: Domain Relational Calculus is a math sentence stating exactly which rows a query should return while saying nothing about how to compute them. Two differently-written queries can then be compared by meaning: if their DRC sentences are provably equivalent, they answer the same question in every possible database, not just the one at hand.

record.label: TFU: three-valued truth
record.statement: TFU is a three-valued truth type (true, false, unknown-which) so that 'we do not know whether the patient had this diagnosis' is a real stored value rather than a missing row. A three-position switch instead of a yes/no toggle forced to guess.

record.label: NaN as unknown measurement
record.statement: Unknown numeric measurements are stored as the floating-point value NaN, chosen deliberately because mathematical reals have no such marker. An absent heart-rate reading becomes a distinguished, checkable value instead of an accident of the database: the form has 'N/A' printed on it rather than a blank the reader must interpret.

record.label: Closed-world assumption as explicit axioms
record.statement: Databases usually treat 'not recorded' as silently false (the closed-world assumption). This system instead writes the assumption down as explicit axioms: every case not explicitly asserted maps to the unknown value. Silence becomes data. The reasoner never has to guess what absence means because absence has been given a name.

record.label: kinets working instructions
record.locator: Whole file: project purpose, ontology-first workflow, core schema classes (Concept, Paper, Finding, Connection, Experiment, ResearchQuestion), Feynman/Einstein explanation rules
record.evidence_description: Defines kinets as a research project on liquid neural networks, connectomics and brain-inspired computing whose discoveries are captured in a LinkML ontology; 'the ontology is the journal, nothing gets lost'.

record.basis: The names collide but the domains differ: kinets studies liquid neural networks and connectomics, the AWS repo simulates biochemical pathway kinetics. The real contrast is over research capture: kinets is ontology-first ('the ontology is the journal, nothing gets lost') while the AWS agent persists nothing across runs, each run minting a fresh uuid with no index. kinets does exactly what the AWS research agent lacks.
